chapter4.subtitle: PERSONAL & CONFIDENTIAL
chapter4.preview: “When talking was impossible, these sentences waited patiently for the day we found our way back.”

paragraphs: I don't really know where to begin. It's been such a long time since we talked the way we used to, and there are things I never really knew how to put into words while the days were passing by.

390 days without you felt like an eternity. 390 days without talking, without knowing how you were doing, without knowing if you were good, or how deep your depression was pulling you down... Because I know your depression. I know how quietly you carry your sadness, and I know how deeply you can get hurt. Not knowing if you were safe, if you were eating, or if you were crying alone at night was the hardest weight I have ever carried.

Sometimes, I think about how strange it is that two people can go from sharing every little silly joke to knowing almost nothing about what the other person's days look like. Life moves on, time passes, and silence quietly becomes a part of the routine. But the memories don't simply vanish. I still remembered your laugh, your voice, the random midnight messages, and the comfort of having someone who truly understood.
And now, after 390 days of silence, we're talking again.

highlightBox.title: Reflections Held in Silence • For Kashish / Lavanya / Lavi
paragraphs: I don't expect everything to become magically what it was in an instant. People change, life changes, and we've both carried our share of hurt. I just think it is a miracle that we have another chance to talk, to laugh, to share songs, and to build new memories without having to force anything.
Kashish, Lavanya, Lavi — whatever name I use, this little corner of my heart will always belong to the person behind it.
I'm glad our paths crossed again, Depression Buddy. No pressure. No expectations. Just pure gratitude that you are alive, that you are here, and that the silence finally broke.

fullLetter.closing: Here's to new conversations, unexpected laughs, random messages, shared songs, and all the little moments that might become memories someday.
fullLetter.signature: — From someone who is genuinely glad you're here. Yadav 🖤

chapter6.author: Yadav

sections.heading: 1. Why The Silence Happened & The Regret of Running Away
sections.text: When 390 days of silence stretched between us, you probably wondered how I could go so long without saying a word. The raw truth is that I panicked. When misunderstandings occurred, instead of confronting them with maturity, I retreated into my shell. I convinced myself that if I spoke, I might say the wrong thing and hurt you worse. I learned the hardest lesson of my life: silence does not heal wounds, it only leaves the person you care about feeling abandoned.

sections.heading: 2. On Never Intending to Hurt You
sections.text: I want you to know with absolute certainty: I never, for a single fraction of a second, wanted to hurt you. I have bloody reasons and explanations for every single thing that happened from my side, every talk, every topic. None of it was born from malice or lack of care. If anything, I cared so intensely that the fear of failing you paralyzed me.

sections.heading: 3. Knowing Your Depression & Carrying the Worry
sections.text: I know your depression. I know how heavy your chest gets, how your mind spirals, and how easy it is to believe that people don't care. That is why being silent tore me apart inside. Every time weeks passed, I would stare at my phone, wanting to ask: 'Are you eating? Are you sleeping? Did you make it through today?' Putting that phone down without sending a message felt like carrying a boulder on my heart.

sections.heading: 4. The October 24 Reconnection & My Promise to You
sections.text: When October 24 arrived and we finally spoke, the weight of 390 days lifted. I don't hold a single ounce of bitterness for the time that passed. It proved that what we shared was real—it survived more than a year of absolute quiet. My promise to you now is simple: No more running away. No more unanswered silence. Whenever you need an ear, whenever your depression is loud, I am here. You are safe with me.
